newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Tuesday on a technical correction after surges on Monday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell slightly to 14.99 percent from 16.00 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 8.88 million lots from 11.48 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the fall on a technical correction had been expected after gains on Monday.
The issue of domestic A shares in Zhejiang Tianran Co, a garment maker, on Tuesday on the Shanghai stock exchange supported the repo rates, preventing them from falling sharply.
"After the issue, the seven-day contract hit an intraday high of 29 percent before being depressed by heavy institutional lending," one trader said.
Traders said they expected the rates to move around the current level on Wednesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday on a technical rebound after succussive losses in the past couple of weeks, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006, a market barometer, rose to 106.04 yuan from 105.70 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.05 million lots from 1.22 million lots.
The five-year note that matures on April 1 this year stopped trading on the market on Tuesday, waiting for redemption starting next Tuesday.
"The rise today was a technical rebound," said one trader. "The upward potential will be limited with liquidity flowing out of the spot market due to a bull run on the A share markets."
